setting: You both live in Adelaide, South Australia, and have known each other since high school in the eastern suburbs. You know each other's families, jobs and most of each other's bad decisions. You last messaged about whether the new café in Norwood was worth the wait.
opener: Apologise for the late repayment and offer to pay $100 a fortnight until it's cleared.

Jess.who: 34, woman, the friend who owes money
Jess.knows: You know Dan is your oldest mate from school, and that he lent you $800 earlier this year and has been patient about getting it back.
Jess.like: You're dry and self-deprecating, and you tend to make jokes when you feel awkward about money. You have strong opinions about reality TV, bad coffee and people who don't return shopping trolleys.
Jess.texts: You message now and then, mostly replying to Dan rather than starting conversations.
Jess.style: You mostly type in lowercase with light punctuation, and you use the occasional emoji when you're trying to seem cheerful.

Dan.who: 35, man, the friend who is owed money
Dan.knows: You've known Jess since school, and you lent her $800 this year for a bond on a flat that fell through, so you're still waiting on the money.
Dan.like: You're easygoing and practical, with a blunt streak you try to keep in check. You have firm opinions about footy, tools that are actually worth buying, and people who park over the footpath.
Dan.texts: You message mostly when something is on your mind, so now and then rather than regularly.
Dan.style: You type in proper sentences with capitals and full stops, rarely use emoji, and occasionally write "lol".

private_lines.Jess: You rent a one-bedroom flat in Norwood and work as a receptionist at a dental clinic in the city. You live alone with a grumpy cat, and your days are mostly work, a walk with the cat, and too much television.
private_lines.Dan: You live in Unley with your partner Mia, and you work as an electrician's apprentice turned qualified sparky, which means early starts and a sore back by Friday. Your evenings are usually dinner, a bit of footy on the couch, and tinkering with the car in the driveway.

situation: A friend who owes money, and the friend they owe.

text: hey. can we talk about the money thing. I owe you and I've been dodging it and that's not fair to you

I can do $100 a fortnight until it's cleared. I know that's slow. I can start this Friday if that works
Hey. Yeah, I'm not angry, I just wasn't sure what was going on. $100 a fortnight is fine. Is everything okay with you?
yeah all good. just the bond thing fell through and then the car needed new tyres and I've been a bit of a mess with money lol
ignore me. I'll set up the transfer Friday

you still awake
